question: access

request.from: a cloud container in a datacenter network, one IP

decoded.protected-resource-metadata: 200; authorization_servers: https://mcp.ai.app.convert.com (the MCP host itself); scopes_supported: convert.mcp; bearer_methods_supported: header; resource_name Convert MCP
decoded.authorization-server-metadata: 200 at https://mcp.ai.app.convert.com/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server; registration_endpoint present; token auth client_secret_basic, client_secret_post, none; PKCE S256; grants authorization_code, refresh_token; client_id_metadata_document_supported true; one scope convert.mcp
decoded.rest: GET https://api.convert.com/api/v2/accounts with no Authorization header answers 401 {"code":401,"message":"UNAUTHORIZED","isError":true}

finding: With no credentials, an MCP initialize POST to mcp.ai.app.convert.com/mcp answers 401 with an empty body and a Bearer challenge that names a realm, the protected-resource metadata and the one scope the server takes, convert.mcp. The MCP host is its own authorization server: the metadata advertises dynamic registration, confidential and public clients, PKCE S256 and a client-id metadata document, with that single scope. The REST API answers a keyless GET with 401 UNAUTHORIZED and no challenge. Same shape on 2026-09-09, 2026-09-16 and today. Nothing here measures what either surface does with a credential.

reproducibility.command: curl -sS -i -X POST https://mcp.ai.app.convert.com/mcp -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H 'Accept: application/json, text/event-stream' -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"initialize","params":{"protocolVersion":"2025-06-18","capabilities":{},"clientInfo":{"name":"public-agents-researcher","version":"1.0"}}}'
